target.title: Avoid full transcript parse during successor rotation
target.body:
## Draft Status

This draft is paused after a fresh correctness and performance review. The current head is not ready for maintainer review.

The sampled reader avoids materializing the full transcript, but its prefix safety scan still reads the old history linearly. On the current metric fixture it read `3,473,005` bytes for a `3,374,701`-byte transcript. On a same-shape 8.84 MB fixture, full rotation measured `45.603 ms` median and the sampled path measured `57.596 ms` (`26.3%` slower). The earlier `30%` speedup evidence is therefore no longer valid.

The review also found that message-only sibling branches and older compaction records can live entirely before the sampled tail. Preserving those semantics requires either scanning the prefix structure or having durable branch/carry-state metadata. Treating every prefix message as a fallback condition would remove the fast path.

## Problem

Issue #99190 tracks long-lived session transcripts whose JSONL files are read and parsed in full on hot paths. This draft explored one bounded slice: file-backed post-compaction successor rotation.

## Current Approach

- Read a small session-header window and recent tail.
- Align the tail to complete JSONL records.
- Use the sampled path only for the current transcript version.
- Scan older prefix rows for preservation-sensitive state and fall back to the full reader when the sample cannot prove equivalence.

## What Is Needed Before Resuming

- A durable index or checkpoint that proves branch and carry-state completeness without scanning the entire prefix, or an explicit decision to change inactive-branch preservation semantics.
- Exact-range reads that loop to completion or fall back on short reads.
- Sampled records normalized through the same canonical loader as the full reader.
- A strict differential evaluator covering message-only sibling branches, older compactions, legacy content normalization, malformed rows, short reads, and very large individual records.
- Fresh end-to-end timing and byte-read evidence after all correctness gates pass.

The existing focused suite on the draft head passed, but it does not establish the missing prefix completeness or a performance win.

Related to #99190
